newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk Q2 net off on lower sales.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk Q2 net off on lower sales.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp Thursday reported second-quarter earnings of $0.22 per share, compared to $0.30 per share a year earlier, citing lower sales and other factors.
The company also said directors declared dividends at prescribed rates for all series of preferred stock.

It said earnings were lower due to several factors, including lower sales of electricity and natural gas, higher independent power producer (IPP) capacity costs, higher electric customer discounts, and higher electric fuel costs that will be recovered next quarter.
Retail sales of electricity were off 0.7 percent in the second quarter, but total electricity sales decreased 7.5 percent, as wholesale sales dropped 38.6 percent during the quarter.
Electric revenues for the second quarter of 1997 were $804.5 million, essentially unchanged from a year earlier.
Although sales of electricity were lower for the quarter, the revenue impact was offset primarily by increased energy payments to IPPs which are recovered through the fuel adjustment clause.

Retail sales of natural gas decreased 1.7 percent in the second quarter as decreases in the commercial and industrial classes more than offset a 1.5 percent increase in residential sales. Total gas deliveries, which include the transportation of customer-owned gas, were up 9 percent.
Natural gas revenues for the second quarter of 1997 were $141.2 million, down 9.7 percent from a year earlier.

Although total gas deliveries increased, gas revenues decreased primarily as a result of the migration of commercial sales customers to the transportation class and the restructuring of gas rates in the company's December 1996 gas rate agreement.
